name: OmniAgent REST API Guidelines
description: REST API guidelines for OmniAgent, based on PlexusOne guidelines but using snake_case for OpenAI API compatibility. All OpenAI-compatible endpoints use snake_case to match the official OpenAI API specification.

principles.title: API First
principles.description: Design and document APIs before implementation. The OpenAPI specification is the contract between teams.

principles.title: Consumer-Centric Design
principles.description: Design APIs from the consumer's perspective. Optimize for the common use cases, not internal implementation.

principles.title: Consistency Over Cleverness
principles.description: Consistent patterns across endpoints reduce cognitive load. Predictable APIs are easier to learn and use.

principles.title: OpenAI API Compatibility
principles.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoints (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/models) follow OpenAI's API conventions including snake_case property names for seamless client library compatibility.

principles.title: Design for Evolution
principles.description: APIs will change. Design for backward compatibility from day one. Never break existing clients.

principles.title: Simplicity
principles.description: Keep APIs simple. Avoid unnecessary complexity. When in doubt, leave it out.

categories.title: Naming Conventions
categories.description: Consistent naming for resources, properties, and URLs

categories.title: HTTP Methods
categories.description: Proper use of HTTP verbs and semantics

rules.title: Provide OpenAPI 3.1 specification
rules.description: All APIs MUST have an OpenAPI 3.1 specification. The spec is the source of truth and MUST be maintained alongside code.
rules.rationale: OpenAPI enables tooling, documentation generation, client SDK generation, and contract testing. Version 3.1 aligns with JSON Schema draft 2020-12.

rules.title: Use snake_case for property names (OpenAI compatibility)
rules.description: All JSON property names MUST use snake_case (e.g., first_name, created_at, user_id) for compatibility with OpenAI API conventions.
rules.rationale: OmniAgent provides OpenAI-compatible APIs. Using snake_case ensures seamless compatibility with existing OpenAI client libraries (openai-python, openai-node, etc.) and reduces friction for developers migrating from OpenAI.

rules.title: Use kebab-case for URL paths
rules.description: URL path segments MUST use kebab-case (lowercase with hyphens) or simple lowercase.
rules.rationale: Kebab-case is the standard for URLs. It's readable and avoids issues with case sensitivity in different systems.

rules.title: Use plural nouns for collection resources
rules.description: Collection resource names MUST be plural nouns. Use /users not /user, /models not /model.
rules.rationale: Plural nouns make it clear you're dealing with a collection. GET /models returns multiple models.

judge.prompt: Check if collection resources use plural nouns
passCriteria: All collection endpoints use plural nouns

rules.title: Version APIs with URI prefix
rules.description: API endpoints SHOULD be versioned using a URI prefix: /v1/, /v2/, etc. Utility endpoints like /health and /docs are exempt.
rules.rationale: URI versioning is simple, explicit, and cacheable. Utility endpoints are version-agnostic by convention.

rules.title: Use standard HTTP methods correctly
rules.description: Use HTTP methods according to their semantics: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (replace), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (remove).
rules.rationale: Correct HTTP method usage enables caching, idempotency guarantees, and predictable behavior.

judge.prompt: Verify HTTP methods are used according to REST semantics
failCriteria: Actions in URL with wrong method

rules.title: Return 201 Created with Location header for POST
rules.description: Successful POST requests that create resources SHOULD return 201 Created with a Location header pointing to the new resource.
rules.rationale: 201 explicitly indicates creation. The Location header enables clients to fetch the created resource without parsing the response body.

rules.title: Use 204 No Content for successful DELETE
rules.description: Successful DELETE requests SHOULD return 204 No Content with an empty body.
rules.rationale: The resource no longer exists, so there's nothing to return. 204 clearly indicates success without a body.

rules.title: Use ISO 8601 for dates and times
rules.description: All date and time values MUST use ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ for timestamps, YYYY-MM-DD for dates.
rules.rationale: ISO 8601 is unambiguous and sortable. Always use UTC (Z suffix) for timestamps to avoid timezone confusion.

rules.title: Use string for IDs
rules.description: Resource identifiers MUST be strings, not integers.
rules.rationale: String IDs are more flexible than integers. They support UUIDs, prefixed IDs, and don't have integer overflow issues.

rules.title: Use Bearer token authentication
rules.description: APIs MUST support Bearer token authentication for OpenAI client library compatibility.
rules.rationale: Bearer tokens are the standard for API authentication. OpenAI client libraries expect Authorization: Bearer headers.

rules.title: Document all endpoints with summary and description
rules.description: Every endpoint MUST have a summary (one line) and description (detailed explanation) in the OpenAPI spec.
rules.rationale: Good documentation reduces support burden and improves developer experience.

rules.title: Define servers in specification
rules.description: The OpenAPI specification MUST define at least one server URL.
rules.rationale: Server URLs enable API clients and documentation tools to know the base URL for requests.

rules.title: Use descriptive operation IDs
rules.description: OpenAPI operationId SHOULD follow the pattern: verbResource (e.g., getModel, createChatCompletion, listAgents).
rules.rationale: Consistent operation IDs enable better SDK generation and documentation.

rules.title: Provide schema descriptions
rules.description: All schemas in components/schemas SHOULD have descriptions explaining their purpose.
rules.rationale: Schema descriptions improve API documentation and help developers understand data structures.

minimum.description: Minimum viable API - basic OpenAI compatibility
